en.t: some of the hard service of
and some of his heavy yoke

02.r: Solomon made the people's burden harsh.
02.n: The causative of a verb meaning to be hard or severe. The same root gives the adjective 'hard' later in the verse.

03.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'our yoke'.

04.r: The burden of labour Solomon laid on them, pictured as a yoke.
04.n: Gesenius: a yoke, a curved piece of wood laid on the neck of beasts for drawing, and mostly used figuratively of servitude, citing 1 Ki. 12:11.

05.r: Turns from the father to the son.
05.n: The pronoun is written out, for emphasis: you, unlike your father.

06.r: The request is for the start of the new reign.

07.r: The people ask for a lighter burden, not its removal.
07.n: An imperative of the causative form of a verb that Gesenius gives first as 'to be light'; so 'make light'.

08.r: Part of the labour Solomon required, not all of it.
08.n: The prefix 'from' here means 'some of': they ask for a part to be lifted. The noun is labour or service; the brief's lexicon lists 'labour, service (of captives or subjects)'. It comes from the same root as 'serve' at the end of the verse.

10.n: Gesenius: hard, used of hard servitude, citing this verse. It agrees with 'service', after it in the Hebrew: 'the service of your father, the hard one'.

11.r: The same yoke, now named as Solomon's.
11.n: The same 'some of' as before 'service', so the request is again for a part. The yoke is the one mentioned at the start of the verse.

12.r: The yoke weighed heavily on them.
12.n: The brief's lexicon gives heavy, and also hard, difficult, burdensome. The same root is Rehoboam's verb in his answer, 'made heavy' (1 Kings 12:14).

13.r: Introduces what Solomon did with the yoke.

14.r: Solomon laid the yoke on them.
14.n: The common verb 'give', used here for putting or laying something on someone.

15.r: On the tribes who are speaking.

s: and we will be your subjects
16.r: Their promise of loyalty, on condition the burden is eased.
16.n: The brief's lexicon lists 'to serve as subjects' among this verb's senses. YLT keeps the plain form: 'and we serve thee'.

02.n: βαρύνω, to make heavy: the Greek says 'made heavy', where the Hebrew says 'made hard'.

04.n: κλοιός, properly a collar, here for the yoke.

08.n: δουλεία, slavery, from δοῦλος, slave: the Greek calls the service slavery.

16.n: δουλεύω, to serve as a slave, from the same root as δουλεία earlier in the verse.
